content.user_title: Build React Frontends With Clear Guidelines
content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent architecture, data fetching, styling, and performance standards. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical React and TypeScript rules.
actual_capabilities: Guides Suspense-first data fetching with TanStack Query patterns.
Defines feature-based folders, API service boundaries, and import aliases.
Provides React component standards for props, hooks, handlers, and exports.
Documents MUI v7 styling, Grid syntax, and layout conventions.
Offers performance guidance for lazy loading, memoization, debounce, and cleanup.
Includes TypeScript rules for explicit types, type imports, and safer interfaces.
limitations: It provides guidance, not runnable automation or project scanning.
It assumes React, TypeScript, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, and MUI conventions.
It does not replace product requirements, backend contracts, or accessibility review.
Some examples need adaptation to local project aliases and component names.

use_cases.title: React Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Build new feature folders with typed APIs, Suspense boundaries, routing, and reusable components.

use_cases.title: Code Review Alignment
use_cases.description: Review React code against shared rules for imports, data fetching, styling, and performance.

use_cases.title: Legacy UI Refactoring
use_cases.description: Move older loaders and inline API calls toward Suspense-first and feature-based patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines. Create a React component for [feature]. Include props, Suspense data fetching, MUI styling, and TypeScript notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Feature Module
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a full feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines. Plan a new [feature] module. Include folder structure, API service boundaries, route setup, and cache strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Review Existing Frontend Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines. Review this React code for architecture, Suspense usage, type safety, MUI v7 syntax, and performance risks.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Complex Data Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use frontend-dev-guidelines. Refactor this page toward cache-first TanStack Query, isolated API services, lazy routes, and smaller focused components.

output_examples.input: Create a user dashboard with stats, active users, and recent activity.
output_examples.output: A component plan using parallel Suspense queries, lazy sections, MUI Grid layout, and typed API service boundaries.

output_examples.input: Review a feature component before merging it.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review covering early loaders, inline API calls, prop drilling, missing type imports, and performance risks.

output_examples.input: Refactor a route file for better loading behavior.
output_examples.output: A route plan with lazy loaded component entry, SuspenseLoader placement, breadcrumb metadata, and feature-based imports.

best_practices: Use the skill before writing new React components or feature modules.
Provide existing file paths, route names, API shapes, and UI requirements.
Ask for a review checklist when changing shared frontend patterns.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a replacement for product requirements or API contracts.
Do not apply every rule blindly to legacy code without migration context.
Do not ask it to bypass project linting, tests, or accessibility checks.

faq.question: What projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits React and TypeScript applications that use Suspense, TanStack Query, TanStack Router, and MUI.

faq.question: Can it generate complete frontend code?
faq.answer: Yes, it can guide component, route, hook, and API service drafts from your requirements.

faq.question: Does it run tests or inspect a repository?
faq.answer: No, it is guidance content. The AI tool must separately read files, edit code, and run tests.

faq.question: Does it require Suspense for all data fetching?
faq.answer: It prefers Suspense-first patterns for new work and allows legacy exceptions with clear context.

faq.question: Can teams customize the rules?
faq.answer: Yes, teams should adapt aliases, route names, API clients, and styling choices to their codebase.

faq.question: Is this skill security sensitive?
faq.answer: It is Markdown guidance. It does not include executable scripts, installers, or background network calls.
